title: What are some of your favorite free ai tools for gamedev?
author: Any-Landscape434
selftext: Just wondering if its possible to start for 100% free without paying nothing? if so what are some solid ai's you enjoy, how do they compare to paid models? ive always wanted to make a game but i lack almost every skill to do so by myself.

comments.author: StandardCategory5153
comments.body: Just get $20 a month Claude use Opus 5.5 connect it to a free GitHub account and start prompting a three.js game anyway you want

replies.author: yaxir
replies.body: whats so great about three.js?

replies.author: Brewgazer
replies.body: If the person has never done any thing game dev related it’s a great place to start without having to download a game engine, they’ll start to wonder about assets and go seeking the information

replies.author: yaxir
replies.body: Thx

replies.author: StandardCategory5153
replies.body: Nah bruv, you can make pretty much any game in three.js. No engine needed.

replies.author: Brewgazer
replies.body: Yes in theory you can but also you can get into godot which is an open source engine that pairs well with Claude, I’m sure me and my team could have built our own engine but with godot because it’s open source you really can make it your own engine which is really nice

replies.author: StandardCategory5153
replies.body:
But why? I seriously haven't found a reason atm.

I'm a pro dev who has shipped a bunch of commercial games over the years with teams. I've used UE4, UE5, Unity, our own proprietary engines as well.

Having used Claude make three.js games with real 3D assets has been amazing. Need a tool? Claude can make whatever bespoke tool you need. Need a look? A renderer? Claude can do that too.

javascript is single thread, so at very large scale games with heavy simulation this could be a problem, but even then you could simply offload some of it in C++ at that point as long as you're aware of it. Which AI can also do no problem.

comments.author: StoneCypher
comments.body: there aren’t any good free ones that i know of, but claude and chatgpt are both great at less than one pizza a month

replies.author: Any-Landscape434
replies.body: ive tried both chatgpt and claude 20 dollars plans before in the past for a brief period, but im not sure what ai i prefer, also what about things like art/models, music, and such?

replies.author: StandardCategory5153
replies.body:
Claude Opus 5.5 is 10x better than older Claude models for programming. It's unreal.

Art... you'll need to either find free assets, buy assets, ask Claude to use free Blender (which will blow through your $20 account) or have Claude make simple art itself. Or use a 3d AI like [meshy.ai](http://meshy.ai)

replies.author: Brewgazer
replies.body: If you give it blender skills it won’t really blow through it too much, it then has rules when using blender so it doesn’t eat as much

replies.author: pol-delta
replies.body: Any particular blender skills you recommend?

replies.author: Brewgazer
replies.body: You want the link to skills or link to a discord that acts like a library for skills and tools some free some paid?

replies.author: pol-delta
replies.body: Either would be great, but especially any that you’ve actually had good experience with. There are tons of skills out there, but it’s hard to know which ones are actually worth it. I appreciate it!

replies.author: Brewgazer
replies.body:
[https://discord.gg/4xqMbscPv](https://discord.gg/4xqMbscPv)

Just ask in there about blender skills

replies.author: OkExperience8139
replies.body:
Depending on your set up id have claude build you a comfy ui based set up using trellis and other tools he will know about , I have a all in one image to 3d render set up each asset takes about  3 minutes from original concept to 3d but I also have a 5090 and i9-14000k cpu 64 gig ram totall.

About 5 months of game development claude opus 5.5 is by miles the best and most cost effective model out there! Codex is like the dumber slower little brother and my local agent eats paint chips.

comments.author: JakSilver00
comments.body: This may come as a surprise to you, but you still need some skills to use the AI tools. Additionally, you don't need any AI tools to actually do game dev. And I don't know what you're considering to start. But yeah, you can technically start for free. There's even free tutorials, free game engines. free assets. So if your only skill is finding things, you could still technically build a game for free.

replies.author: StandardCategory5153
replies.body: You can't use free tiers of AI LLMs to code. They're purposefully stupid.

replies.author: JakSilver00
replies.body: Yeah, no, I've done it and there are special models that are still freely available. You just have to find them.

replies.author: StandardCategory5153
replies.body: Like local LLMs? Sure. I don’t find it worth it to not pay though.

comments.body: This may come as a surprise to you, but you still need some skills to use the AI tools. Additionally, you don't need any AI tools to actually do game dev. So if your only skill is finding things, you could still technically build a game for free.

comments.author: kakashi_sakurai
comments.body:
If you don’t know anything, you still need to learn everything. Ai cannot magically do everything for you and produce anything that isn’t either awful or just soulless. 

Take of free online courses or something on game development.

replies.author: StandardCategory5153
replies.body:
Nah. AI can magically do everything for you. Art. Sound. Music. Code. Balancing. UI. Networking. QA. Localization. Story writing.

It won't be GOOD. It'll be terrible slop, because AI has no idea what is good or bad to a human.... That requires taste, talent and skill.   
  
But it will be a finished game that one can play.

replies.author: Friendly-Beginning72
replies.body:
not of a fan of this idea, nor following it but here's a different perspective:  
\- you do something with AI. it ends up awful / soulless  
\- you get some traffic (somehow)  
\- you go trial and error (with AI) blindly to see what works in terms of features/art and choose the best result every time. something like A/B testing  
\- repeat the last step

replies.author: StandardCategory5153
replies.body:
You just described ACTUAL game dev. :)

How it used to be:  
You make a prototype it looks like trash because no final art.   
It plays super duper rough because it has no user feedback yet.   
Some people play it, you iterate  
You make the final product

A lot of ai sloppers won't have the time or patience for this though. The last 10% of your game is usually 90% of the work.

replies.author: Friendly-Beginning72
replies.body: not necessarily. i would say that in the older process you would do your best before launching. ofc you get feedback along the way, but limited usually

replies.author: Friendly-Beginning72
replies.body:
here's one example i recently saw on itch: somebody had an idea of a small puzzle game (the idea was not bad, the execution was clearly just 1 prompt / 0 effort).  
clearly all levels were similar (almost identical in playing all 20 levels of the game).  
  
i gave some feedback about it and 30 minutes later i got the answer: "here's 150 levels with the variations you asked for".

1 prompt for the game and another copy-paste of a feedback comment and he ended up with a slightly better game. then repeat 50 times. 0 effort, 0 f&\^& given about the game itself from the developer.

comments.author: COLES-BRAND-NUTMEG
comments.body:
If by game dev you include modding, I built the prototype for my upcoming Mount & Blade total combat AI overhaul (absolutely blasting away the original AI) with whatever model pops up when you type a question in google. You can do a lot for free.

So long my friend - we got a lot done!

comments.author: wavy_d3
comments.body: Mine is [shinygen.ai](http://shinygen.ai) it's an AI game maker that lets you create GBC, GBA, N64, DS, Gamecube, and Godot games with AI. Has AI built-in and let's you bring your own AI. You can actually export the console roms and export your games too. Runs on web, android, ios.
